vocabulary.definition: an authoritarian government headed by a hereditary monarch
hatred and prejudice directed at people of Jewish faith or origin
classic; the example on which others are based
an act of violence or cruelty that viewed as exceptionally shocking due to its nature or extent
economic self-sufficiency
an approach to government in which the leadership is not elected by or accountable to the people it governs.
a legislature that is comprised of two legislative "houses", both of which must approve a bill before it becomes law
a proposed law under consideration by the government

Classical liberalism emphasizes individual freedom, private property, competition, economic freedom, and limited government. It is resisted when people believe these principles create inequality, exploitation, poverty, instability, or neglect of collective needs.

in a parliamentary system, the term used to describe a situation where two or more rival parties agree to work together, combining the seats they have won in an election in order to have sufficient total seats to form the government
The abolition of private property in favour of group or state ownership

Communism rejects many liberal economic and political principles by seeking classless society, collective ownership, and the end of capitalism. In practice, communist states have often used strong state power and limited individual freedoms.
the forceful overthrow of a government by a small group of individuals
the negative value obtained when expenditures exceed income
an authoritarian system in which power is concentrated in the hands of a single person; autocracy
a person who disagrees with the government
the citizens within a population who are eligible to vote
the freeing of enslaved or indentured people
a largely discredited science of improving the human race through programs of selective breeding, sterilization and euthanasia

Fascism rejects liberalism by emphasizing ultranationalism, authoritarian leadership, obedience, militarism, and the subordination of individual rights to the state or nation. It often treats dissent and pluralism as threats.
a system of government under which power is divided between the national government and provincial, state or territorial governments
see suffrage
a government policy that promotes the establishment of an empire, usually through military conquest
an oligarchy formed by a committee of military officers
in a parliamentary system, the term used to describe a situation where the governing party has more than 50% of the available seats in the legislature
a government policy that promotes the development and maintenance of a powerful military in order to protect and promote a country's national interests
in a parliamentary system, the term used to describe a situation where the governing party more seats than any other party in the legislature, but has less than 50% of the total seats
a form of oligarchy in which the government is operated by, and in the interests of, a minority group within the population
literally “new-liberalism”; an economic philosophy that returns to many of the basic economic ideals laid out by classical liberal economist like Adam Smith
an authoritarian system in which power is concentrated in the hands a small ruling group or committee
an adjective used to describe a private army or unofficial militia
a Russian word meaning restructuring
A plebiscite is an expression of public opinion, it is advisory only and not binding on government, whether federal, provincial or municipal.
the percentage of the total votes cast received by a candidate or a political party
a liberal movement of the early 20th century that sought political, economic and social reform in the United States.
term given to the supply-side economic policies instituted under the administration of U.S. President Ronald Reagan in the 1980s.
a political process by which the electorate, by way of new election outside of the time frame of regular general elections, may reverse a previous decision to elect an individual to public office

a direct vote by the electorate on an issue of importance. A referendum is usually (unless non-binding) legally binding verdict of the people which must be acted upon by the government in the form of a law.
a system under which individuals elected to government represent roughly similar numbers of citizens
the constitutional right of a level of government to legislate matters not explicitly referred to in the constitution.

Resistance to liberalism means challenging, rejecting, limiting, or modifying liberal principles such as individual rights, private property, competition, self-interest, rule of law, or limited government. Resistance can come from citizens, social movements, governments, or competing ideologies.
the provision that voters should be able to cast their ballot in private and that no other individual should have knowledge of how they voted unless the voter wishes to inform them.
an electoral system in which the winning candidate is the one who receives the highest number of votes: also called first-past-the-post
a system under which a single individual represents the citizens of a riding or constituency

Socialism emphasizes cooperation, public ownership or strong public control, economic equality, and collective responsibility. It often resists economic liberalism because it argues that unregulated markets can produce inequality and exploitation.
a situation in which an economy appears to be in recession but is still subject to rising prices and wage demands
the right to vote; also the franchise
a economic school of thought that advocates reducing taxes, especially for the wealthy, and reducing government regulation in the economy.
term used to describe a dictatorship or oligarchy which attempts to impose its control and ideological beliefs on all aspects of society
praise for, and promotion of, the values and achievements of the past

the concept that, under a supply-side approach to economics, tax breaks for the wealthy would encourage investment and create jobs, thereby allowing wealth to “trickle-down” to the middle and lower classes
Republic: a term used to describe the democratic government that existed in Germany between 1919 and 1933

Welfare capitalism keeps many liberal economic features, such as markets and private property, but accepts government programs and regulation to reduce hardship and protect citizens. It is a modification of liberalism rather than a complete rejection.
